summary: Winbond's second 12-inch wafer fab, in the Kaohsiung Science Park at Luzhu, Kaohsiung, making specialty DRAM. Construction began in October 2018 and finished in 2021; the board approved about NT$13.1 billion of capital spending in March 2021, and the fab began mass production in 2022, later than the 2021 target set at groundbreaking. The first module, Module A, ran about 16,000 wafers a month in the third quarter of 2026 with a target of about 24,000 by the end of that year. Winbond plans a second module, Module B, for 50,000 to 60,000 wafers a month; in November 2026 its board approved about NT$73.2 billion for the building, facilities and long-lead tools, with a groundbreaking planned for 29 December 2026, first shipments in the second half of 2029 and full output in 2030.

notes: Trade press calls Module B the P2 fab or the second phase (KH9B, with Module A as KH9A); this record keeps it as a phase of the Kaohsiung fab because Winbond presented it as an expansion of that fab. The Module B plans come from news and trade press reports of company statements and of the November 2026 board decision; no Winbond release or board filing for Module B was read. Reports differ on Module B's process: August 2026 reports named 14nm and 12nm with EUV, November 2026 reports 16nm and 20nm.

review.changes: Added November 2026 reports of the board's NT$73.2 billion Module B capital spending, the planned 29 December 2026 groundbreaking, 16nm process, the 50,000 to 60,000 wafer plan and Module A's third-quarter capacity, updated the status date and summary, and loosened the early-2029 tool move-in date to the year.
